statusHistory.note: San Francisco Tier 1 queue (content/post-plan.md), war-room slate 2026-08-31, drafted via near-write-article. Rotation: NEXT-UP was San Francisco per content-rotation/SKILL.md, cycle 2. Dedupe check: grepped content/places/ for dolphin/aquatic-park, no existing pin, this is net-new. Trust 'auto': queue item, war-room-verified slate, independently re-verified this session rather than trusted blind. VERIFICATION FINDINGS: (1) FEE CORRECTED — the queue note said ~$10; the club's own current visit page (dolphinclub.org/visit) states $12 cash/check, $12.67 by card, which is what's published here, with the drift from $10 called out explicitly in-body rather than silently overwritten (older aggregators — National Geographic, Secret San Francisco, a stale search snippet citing $10 — still carry the older figure). This is a price-drift catch, not a structural change: still walk-up, no membership/sponsorship required, so the trust gate holds. (2) HOURS confirmed current: Mon/Wed/Fri, 9am-5pm Nov-Apr, 8am-5pm May-Oct, no holidays, per the same official visit page. (3) 1877 FOUNDING confirmed via Wikipedia and the club's own site; the 1906-earthquake angle from the assignment brief was checked and DROPPED — no source (Wikipedia, Openwaterpedia, general SF-earthquake retrospectives) connects the club specifically to earthquake/fire history, so it's excluded rather than implied. Women's admission (1976 suit, 1977 admitted, ~40% of ~2,000 members now) is sourced to Wikipedia and stated as such. (4) ALTERNATE-DAYS ARRANGEMENT WITH SOUTH END CONFIRMED, with correction: the clubs do NOT share one building (an early search summary suggested they did) — they occupy separate, adjacent clubhouses at 502 and 500 Jefferson St, per Openwaterpedia and general club-history sources. What's real: Dolphin Club takes public guests Mon/Wed/Fri, South End Rowing Club takes Tue/Thu/Sat, so between the two the cove has guest access most weekdays — this is the actual 'alternate days' fact, stated precisely in-body rather than the vaguer 'shared building' framing the slate implied. (5) DATED EVENT: found the Dolphin Club's members-only 'Escape from Alcatraz' race (Sept 12, 2026, days out from this draft — too near-term and members-only to be the piece's hook) and the New Year's Day Alcatraz swim, an annual 40-year tradition, member race but free to watch from the beach, next running January 1, 2027 — used this one per the standing further-out-date preference and because it's genuinely open to the public as a spectator event even though the swim itself is members-only. (6) UGC/REDDIT: searched r/sanfrancisco and general Reddit for a guest account; nothing came back with a linkable, dateable source (search results kept surfacing Wikipedia/NatGeo instead of actual threads). Yelp reviews were blocked (403) from direct fetch. Per the anti-fabrication rule, no UGC quote is used in this piece rather than inventing one — logged as an open gap rather than papered over. IMAGES: hero is the clubhouse facade (Dolphin_club_front.jpg, Neal Mueller, CC BY-SA 4.0, March 2020) — a real source photo, tier 1, no faces. In-body Figure is a beach-view shot of both clubhouses together (Pax Ahimsa Gethen/Funcrunch, CC BY-SA 4.0, Sept 2017), which also supplied precise coordinates (37.808433, -122.421055) used here in place of a manual approximation. Both verified to exist and licensed via direct Commons file-page fetch, not assumed from a filename guess. RESEARCH FLOOR: near-deep-researcher-style multi-source pass across the club's own site, South End's site, Wikipedia, National Geographic, Openwaterpedia, and race-registration sites; fewer than five content/preferred-sources.md entries existed for this specific subject going in, which is itself the finding — San Francisco's outdoors/wellness beat has a thin source catalogue outside the venue's own site and Wikipedia. New sources (dolphinclub.org, serc.com, openwaterpedia.com) logged to content/preferred-sources.md candidates. Operator ground-truth check: not applicable, outside the Baixada Santista/SP/Rio scope this session covers.
